scope.title: Spec Studio
scope.framing: The Spec Studio of the original design, `docs/lineage/v0-design/07-spec-studio-and-projections.md` sections 1 to 3, 11 and 12, in the order a reviewer reads it: what the Studio is and why it renders HTML; the data it reads, with the recipe answers it composes and its two named inputs, and the verb that publishes and watches it; its shell, search and navigation; its four lenses, with the index that is the Packs lens and the coverage recipe the tests lens reads; the Pack page and its maturity map; the Spec page with its core and its panels; the register pages, the owner queue, and the diff, runs and glossary pages, with the run-evidence recipe the runs page reads; the composing panel and the memo it hands off; its custom elements, the decisions that shape them, and the diagrams the engine draws for them; its phone layout; the Pack export and print; how a build is stamped and shared; and the skill that teaches an agent to publish, share and read the Studio and to apply what a person composes in it. Each Spec is followed by the examples that will verify it. Recipe 27, references into a design, shows each member's code bindings and the implemented Specs it builds on.

members.title: The Spec Studio is a static HTML workbench over the one graph
The Studio renders HTML, and the HTML stays derived
The Studio renders from the reader's values and embeds only what its script reads
A page takes each recipe answer from the recipe's shipped body
The Studio reads two named inputs beside the graph, a base graph and run records
Without inputs the page set is the graph's alone
Both inputs add their pages, named, and the same inputs write the same bytes
`sdp studio` publishes the Studio as one page set
`sdp studio --watch` rebuilds the page set on each carrier change
Each watch cycle writes the page set a plain run writes
The Studio's shell frames every page with navigation, a rail and a canvas
Search finds a Spec, a Pack, an entry or a bound file by a word
Every page of the page set is reached from the top navigation and the index
Four lenses read the graph as Packs, architecture, tests and evidence
The Packs lens groups every Spec by the Packs that hold it
The index says where the corpus stands and narrows every Spec
The architecture lens draws components by context and layer, the planned beside the built
A component design no anchor realizes draws planned beside the built one
The tests lens shows how far each Spec's verification reaches
A Spec's row on the tests lens counts its exercised keyed rules
Example spaces report which values their examples cover
A literal no example binds is reported uncovered, and an unbound child is named
A number slot is not enumerable and reports no uncovered value
The evidence lens names each source of runtime evidence and reads it as not tracked
A Pack page shows the Pack's design as one card per member
A Pack page's maturity map places every member by its stated rung and its floor
A Spec page shows one Spec in collapsible panels, in a fixed order
A pinned declaration shows the test line that cites it
A Spec page's core shows the whole Spec, with an anchor for every entry
The panels for examples, targets, verifiers and evidence
Each keyed rule shows the examples that exercise it, or that none does
The corpus's registers are pages a reviewer opens from a link
The questions page lists the Specs with a blocking question first
The owner queue page orders the statements and questions only a person can settle
The owner queue lists a waiting statement after the one it rests on
The diff page shows what changed in the design since a base graph
The diff page shows a changed entry's base and built values
The runs page shows the run records the build was given, joined to test files
The runs page shows a run as external evidence from a test file
CI run records are joined to verifiers in a view
A test whose reporter wrote an absolute path joins its anchored file
A test in a file with no test anchor is reported as unjoined
The glossary page lists every term the corpus's Specs define
A word two Specs define appears once per Spec on the glossary page
A composing panel on every page gathers scoped intent for an agent
Refreshing a tab keeps every gathered intent
Recipe 49 renders a change proposal as the Markdown memo a person reviews
Recipe 49 and the composing panel write one memo for one proposal
The Studio's custom elements each hold one view the build renders
The Studio is built from custom elements, not a framework
The build renders every Studio view, and an element only enhances it
The engine lays out every Studio diagram as static SVG when the page set is built
A diagram is laid out from graph values into SVG with a text equivalent
An architecture within the bound draws in one diagram, the same bytes twice
An architecture over the bound folds by context
One context over the bound folds by layer
A few custom elements filter, search, open and copy on a rendered page
The Studio reads on a phone as on a desktop
A Pack exports as one file, and every page prints as a document
A Pack's export opens alone and keeps its links inside it
A Studio build is stamped and shared from a static host
The stamp is written beside the page set, and a later build removes it
The Studio skill teaches agents to publish, share and read the Spec Studio

questions.question: How does a view say a run is stale: by its commit against the commit being read, or by whether the bound files changed between the two?
questions.provisional: Display the run and source commit identifiers when they differ, as the differing-commit rule requires; whether freshness also follows changes to bound files remains open.
